**PREAMBLE & SHORT TITLE (Sec. 1–2)**
- **Short Title:** Act cited as “Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2024.”
- **Table of Contents:** Lists Divisions A–G. Div. A is the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2024 (Titles I–VIII). Other divisions cover Financial Services, Homeland Security, Labor/HHS/Education, Legislative Branch, State/Foreign Operations, and Other Matters.

**REFERENCES (Sec. 3)**
- Any reference to “this Act” within a division refers only to that division’s provisions. (1 USC 1 note.)

**EXPLANATORY STATEMENT (Sec. 4)**
- The House Appropriations Chair’s explanatory statement (printed ~March 22, 2024, in the Congressional Record) has effect for allocation of funds and implementation of Divs. A–F as if it were a joint explanatory statement of a conference committee.

**STATEMENT OF APPROPRIATIONS (Sec. 5)**
- Sums in the Act are appropriated from the Treasury’s general fund for FY ending Sept. 30, 2024.

**AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS (Sec. 6)**
- Amounts designated by Congress as an emergency requirement under §251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 are available (or repurposed, rescinded, transferred) only if the President subsequently designates all such amounts and transmits those designations to Congress.

**ADJUSTMENTS TO COMPENSATION (Sec. 7)**
- Notwithstanding any other law, no cost-of-living adjustment for Members of Congress under §601(a) of the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 (2 U.S.C. 4501) shall be made during FY2024. (2 USC 4501 note.)

**DIVISION A — Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 2024 (Sections 8058–8150)**

- **Sec. 8058 – Military Family Housing Maintenance Prohibition**
  - Prohibits use of DOD appropriations for repairs/maintenance to DOD military family housing units, including areas used for official business.

- **Sec. 8059 – Defense Innovation Acceleration Reporting & Waiver**
  - New start defense innovation acceleration or rapid prototyping projects >$5M under RDT&E, Defense-Wide require 15-day advance report to congressional defense committees (description, acquisition/transition strategy, annual/total cost estimates) before obligation.
  - Secretary of Defense may waive restriction case-by-case by certifying national interest to committees.

- **Sec. 8060 – Classified Quarterly Reports**
  - Requires Secretary of Defense to continue providing classified quarterly reports to House/Senate Appropriations Committees and Defense Subcommittees on matters directed in the classified annex.

- **Sec. 8061 – National Guard Ballistic Missile Defense Support**
  - Overrides 10 U.S.C. § 12310(b): National Guard members on full-time duty under 32 U.S.C. § 502(f) may perform duties supporting ground-based elements of the National Ballistic Missile Defense System.

- **Sec. 8062 – Armor Piercing Ammunition Transfer Restriction**
  - Prohibits transfer of DOD-held center-fire ammunition designated “armor penetrator,” “AP,” “API,” or “API-T” to non-governmental entities, except to demilitarization contractors that render projectiles non-reusable or manufacture ammunition under DOD contract/export license.

- **Sec. 8063 – National Guard Bureau Lease Waiver**
  - Chief of National Guard Bureau may waive consideration otherwise required under 10 U.S.C. § 2667 for leases of personal property ≤1 year to organizations under 32 U.S.C. § 508(d) or approved youth/social/fraternal nonprofits on a case-by-case basis.

- **Sec. 8064 – Operation & Maintenance, Army Transfer Authority**
  - Makes $175,943,968 from O&M, Army available until expended.
  - Authorizes transfer to other Federal activities; contracts for real property, construction, personal services, operations; indemnification as Secretary determines necessary.
  - Projects must comply with applicable law to maximum extent consistent with national security as determined by Secretary.

- **Sec. 8065 – National Intelligence Program (NIP) Budget Structure Protection**
  - Prohibits modifying NIP appropriations account structure, budget presentation (P-1/R-1/O-1), apportionment processes, or allotment/obligation/disbursement processes.
  - Permits program mergers/changes at or below Expenditure Center level.
  - DNI and SECDEF may jointly study alternative financial management processes for auditable financial statements; must include counterintelligence risk assessment.
  - Requires proposed alternatives to be certified by all affected agencies (helps auditability, improves reporting, no adverse CI effect) and presented to defense/intelligence committees within 30 days of certifications.

- **Sec. 8066 – Africa & Southern Command Cooperation Funds**
  - Appropriates $100M for transfer to O&M, procurement, RDT&E accounts for AFRICOM/SOUTHCOM efforts to expand cooperation, share information, advance interoperability, improve allied/partner capabilities.
  - Requires 30-day advance execution plan and 15-day advance notification

**Part 7 Notes**

**Sec. 238 (Head Start – Indian Tribes)**
- **Purpose/Mechanism:** Authorizes Indian tribes operating Head Start programs to establish their own selection criteria, overriding standard income eligibility requirements.
- **Changes to Law:** Overrides 42 USC 9840 (section 645 of the Head Start Act) income eligibility subsections and regulations.
- **Scope:** Allows prioritization of children from families/households with a tribal member. Applies “In this fiscal year and each fiscal year thereafter.”

**Sec. 239 (Head Start – Migrant/Seasonal Farmworkers)**
- **Purpose/Mechanism:** Authorizes agencies operating migrant/seasonal Head Start programs to establish alternative selection criteria, overriding income eligibility requirements.
- **Changes to Law:** Overrides 42 USC 9840 (section 645(a) of the Head Start Act) income eligibility.
- **Condition:** Enrollment is limited to children with at least one family member whose income is primarily from agricultural employment as defined in 29 U.S.C. 1802 (Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act). Priority must be given to children of migrant farmworker families.

**Sec. 240 (Rescission – Nonrecurring Expenses Fund)**
- **Action:** Rescinds $1,250,000,000 of unobligated balances from the “Nonrecurring Expenses Fund” (established in P.L. 110-161, Div. G, sec. 223).
- **Deadline:** Rescission must occur not later than September 30, 2024.

**Sec. 241 (Rescission – HHS Children and Families)**
- **Action:** Rescinds $70,000,000 of unobligated balances from P.L. 117-328, Div. H, under “Administration for Children and Families—Children and Families Services Programs” for incentive payment grants to states under section 473A of the Social Security Act.

**Working Notes on Operative Provisions (Part 11/11)**

**Sec. 7046. Independent States of the Former Soviet Union**
- **Purpose/Mechanism:** Imposes conditions and prohibitions on assistance to Independent States of the former Soviet Union.
- **Exceptions to Prohibition on Direct Funding (a):** Lists six categories of assistance not subject to a direct funding prohibition: (1) assistance under FREEDOM Support Act title V or Defense Against WMD Act sec. 1424 (50 U.S.C. 2333) or non-proliferation assistance; (2) Trade and Development Agency assistance under Foreign Assistance Act sec. 661; (3) activities of U.S. and Foreign Commercial Service members in official capacity; (4) U.S. International Development Finance Corporation assistance under the BUILD Act of 2018; (5) Export-Import Bank Act financing; (6) humanitarian assistance.
- **Territorial Integrity (b):** Prohibits funds for a government of an Independent State directing action violating territorial integrity/national sovereignty of another (e.g., Helsinki Final Act violations). Exception: President may waive if in U.S. national security interest, except as provided in sec. 7047(a). Condition: Secretary of State must consult Appropriations Committees prior to exercising waiver.
- **Turkey (c):** Prohibits funds to facilitate/support defense article/service sales to Turkish Presidential Protection Directorate (TPPD) under Arms Export Control Act ch. 2 (22 U.S.C. 2761 et seq.) unless Secretary of State determines/reports to appropriate congressional committees that indicted TPPD members (per July 17, 2017, D.C. Superior Court indictment) have returned to the U.S. for trial or been brought to justice. Exception: Limitation does not apply to funds for border security, NATO/coalition operations, or protection of U.S. officials/facilities in Turkey.
- **Ukraine (d):**
    - **Strategy (1):** Deadline: 60 days post-enactment. Secretary of State, coordinating with other agencies, must submit a strategy to congressional leadership and appropriations committees prioritizing U.S. national security interests in response to Russian aggression in Ukraine. Must include goals, benchmarks, timelines, strategic objectives for Ukraine assistance funds, and staffing requirements.
    - **Cost Matching (2):** Limits Economic Support Fund and Assistance for Europe, Eurasia and Central Asia contributions to the Government of Ukraine to 50% of total assistance from all sources. Waiver: President may waive if in national security interest, with detailed justification and explanation of other donors' inability to meet the level. Reporting: Following waiver, President must report every 120 days on steps to increase other donor contributions. Duration: Requirement effective until funds expended.
    - **Oversight (3):**
        - **Staffing (A):** Funds under titles I and II available for appropriate staffing levels in Ukraine/neighboring countries for monitoring, oversight, and security.
        - **In-Person Monitoring (B):** Secretary of State shall ensure project-based assistance for Ukraine under specified headings is subject to in-person monitoring by U.S. personnel or vetted third parties.
        - **Certification (C):** Deadline: 15 days prior to initial obligation. Secretary of State and USAID Administrator must jointly certify/report that monitoring and oversight mechanisms are in place to prevent waste, fraud, abuse, diversion, and corruption. Sec. 7015(e) applies.
        - **Notification (D):** Requirements of sec. 1706 of the Additional Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2023 (division M, Public Law 117-328) apply to Ukraine assistance funds under titles I-IV.
        - **Reports (E):** (i) Deadline: 60 days post-enactment, every 90 days until funds expended. Comprehensive report on Ukraine assistance since Feb. 24, 2022, including unobligated, obligated but unexpended, and committed but unnotified funds, disaggregated by account and fiscal year. (ii) Deadline: 90 days post-enactment, every 90 days until funds expended. Joint report on FY2024 Ukraine assistance uses/planned uses, results, donor contributions, metrics, coordination with IGs, and accounting of waste/fraud/abuse allegations.
        - **Transparency (F):** Reports must be made publicly available consistent with sec. 7016(b).
